The average flow from the project area is estimated at 5 cfs, with a 7Q10 low flow of 0.9 cfs. For the Howard Creek Basin, average flow is estimated at 32 cfs with a 7Q10 low flow of 5.8 cfs (Dysart, et al., 1973). By this analysis, the flow from the project area represents about 16 percent of the Howard Creek Basin flow. Based on the available measured data (Sigmon and Dysart, 1975), the average flow of West Bad and Bad Creeks for the period of April 1973 to June 1975 averaged about 7.7 cfs while at station H1 the average flow was about 47.7 cfs.
Water Quality
The water of streams in the Howard Creek Basin including Bad Creek and West Bad Creek is of high quality and purity in most regards, having similar characteristics at most stations throughout the basin. Water temperatures reach lows of 4° to 5° C throughout the basin, maximum temperatures range from about 17" to 19° C. The maximum temperature of 20.4° C was recorded in Corbin Creek in July of 1973. Dissolved Oxygen (DO) concentrations were almost always above 90 percent of air saturation, ranging from a low of 8.1 ppm at station Hll (July 1973) to 13.3 ppm at station H7 (December 1974). Stream waters are low in alkalintity (3.2  to  8.6  mg/l), appearing mainly in the form of the bicarbonate ion. With such low alkalinity values, these waters are poorly buffered and could be subject to sudden pH changes by the addition of acidic or basic substances. Hardness is also low (calculated mean values for calcium/magnesium hardness of less than 2.0 mg/l reported as calcium carbonate), indicating that the water is very soft (Dwifor and Becker, 1964 as cited by Hem, 1970; Dysart, et al., 1973). Specific conductance (an indirect measure of dissolved solids) values ranged from 3.5 to 21 micromhos/cm for the Howard Creek Basin stations, thereby indicating low levels of dissolved substances in the water. Using conductance values, dissolved solids values were calculated to average about 12 to 15 mg/l (Iseman, et al., 1975).
The pH of the waters in the Howard Creek Basin averages about 6.5 indicating that the water is slightly acidic. Hydrogen ion concentrations varied considerably over the period sampled, with a minimum value of 4.8 at station H9 and a maximum 7.7 at station H7, both extremes being recorded on July 18, 1974. A number of pH values of less than 6.0 are noted for 1974 sampling data, particularly in Bad Creek and West Bad Creek. For a nearly maximum level of protection to fish and aquatic life, pH levels should not exceed 8.5 nor be less than 6.5 (National Academy of Sciences, et al., 1972).
